# 智能合约审计与形式化验证流水线

## 用途

合约产物与 ABI 管理、静态规则与模式库、符号执行与模糊测试编排、不变式检查、缺陷归因与报告版本化。

本仓库是可持续演进的自托管 Go 应用。领域核心位于 `contractsentinel/`，命令入口位于 `cmd/contractsentinel/`。

```bash
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel demo
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel version
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel resolve <config-file> < request.json
go test ./...
```

## 离线路由解析（resolve）

`resolve` 从配置文件读取路由，从标准输入读取一个 JSON 请求，在本机离线
完成匹配并输出命中的路由与上游地址，全程不建立网络连接。

配置文件：

```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"id": "api",  "methods": ["GET"], "pathPrefix": "/api", "upstream": "http://api.internal/v1"},
    {"id": "root", "methods": ["*"],  "pathPrefix": "/",    "upstream": "https://fallback.internal/base/"}
  ]
}
```

请求（`target` 为带可选查询串的路径）：

```json
{"method": "GET", "target": "/api/orders/7?a=1&a="}
```

成功时标准输出：

```json
{"routeId":"api","upstreamURL":"http://api.internal/v1/orders/7?a=1&a="}
```

匹配规则：

- `methods` 为非空数组，元素是区分大小写的具体 HTTP 方法名或 `*`（匹配任意合法方法）。
- `pathPrefix` 以 `/` 开头，除根前缀 `/` 外不能以 `/` 结尾，不含查询串或片段。
- 前缀按原始编码与请求路径匹配，并必须落在路径段边界上：`/api` 匹配
  `/api` 与 `/api/orders`，不匹配 `/apiv2`；`%2F` 不视为分隔符。
- 查询串不参与匹配。多条命中时最长前缀优先；前缀相同则具体方法优先于 `*`；
  仍有多条候选时返回 `route_conflict`，候选 `id` 按字典序排列；无候选返回
  `route_not_found`。
- 命中后去掉请求路径前缀，剩余路径接到 upstream 基础路径之后，连接处恰好
  保留一个 `/`（剩余路径为空也保留）；根前缀 `/` 保留其后全部路径。连接处
  以外的路径、百分号编码与原始查询串（含重复参数、空值与顺序）逐字节保留。

### queryTransforms 查询串改写

每条路由可新增 `queryTransforms` 数组，在路由选定之后、路径拼接完成后按
数组顺序改写查询串；匹配、冲突判定与路径拼接均不受其影响。省略该字段或给
空数组时，原始查询串逐字节保留。规则形如：

```json
"queryTransforms": [
  {"op": "set",    "name": "a",    "value": ""},
  {"op": "remove", "name": "flag"},
  {"op": "rename", "name": "old",  "to": "new"}
]
```

- `op` 仅支持 `set`、`remove`、`rename`；`name` 为非空字符串，按字面值使用。
- `set` 必须提供字符串 `value`（允许空字符串）；`remove` 不接受 `value`。
- `rename` 必须提供非空字符串 `to`，不接受 `value`；`name` 与 `to` 按
  字面值使用。命中的参数在原位置改名，各自的值、数量与相对顺序保留；
  已经叫目标名的参数继续保留，不合并也不覆盖。无等号的参数改名后仍无
  等号，空值保留等号；只重新编码被改动参数的名称（编码方式与 `set`
  相同），等号及其后的内容逐字节保留，值中的 `+`、百分号转义、额外等号
  与大小写都不改写。例如 `old=1&new=9&%6Fld=%2f+&old&x=` 把 `old`
  改名为 `new` 后得到 `new=1&new=9&new=%2f+&new&x=`。没有来源参数时
  查询串完全不变；`name` 与 `to` 相同时也不改写已有的名称编码。
- 查询串只以 `&` 分隔，第一个 `=` 分开名称和值；没有 `=` 的片段也能按名称
  命中。空查询串（`?` 后为空）视为没有片段，其余空片段（如 `?a=1&` 末尾）
  保留且不作为参数。
- 比较参数名称时解码百分号转义、把 `+` 视为空格、区分大小写，不做其他
  归一化；未命中名称的参数与其原始内容、顺序保持不变。
- `remove` 删除该名称的全部参数。`set` 把该名称的全部参数合并为一个，
  放在首次命中的位置；原查询中不存在时追加到末尾。没有查询串时 `remove`
  不产生问号，`set` 会创建查询串；原先的空问号在没有实际修改时保留，
  删除命中参数后若参数与空片段均已清空则去掉问号。
- 新增或替换的参数写成编码后的 `name=value`：仅 ASCII 字母、数字及
  `-._~` 原样出现，其他 UTF-8 字节使用大写百分号转义，空格写为 `%20`。
- 后一条规则基于前一条规则的结果执行。例如查询串
  `x=%2f&a=1&%61=2&flag` 先 `set a=""` 再 `remove flag`，结果为
  `x=%2f&a=`。`rename` 同样按数组次序串接：后续对目标名的 `set`
  仍合并所有同名参数，`remove` 仍删除全部同名参数。

数组或规则为 `null`、字段类型错误、未知操作、空名称、缺少必要字段、
`remove` 带 `value` 或 `rename` 缺少/带非法 `to` 或带 `value`，都使
整个配置返回 `invalid_config`（即使出错路由不会被命中）；reason 定位到
路由，规则错误另给出从 1 开始的规则序号。

失败时标准错误输出含 `code`、`reason` 的 JSON（`route_conflict` 另含
`candidates`），退出状态非零，标准输出不留下结果：

- `invalid_config`：配置不可读、JSON 无效或任一路由不合法（含非法
  queryTransforms；能定位时指出第几条路由及 id，规则错误指出规则序号）。
  合法 JSON 但结构不符与语法损坏严格区分：最外层必须是 JSON 对象，
  数组、字符串、数字、布尔值和 null 都被拒绝，reason 说明配置必须是
  对象并指出实际收到的类型，不猜测路由序号；对象中只要提供 `routes`
  就必须是数组，其他类型（含 null）报 `routes` 类型错误，不能当成没有
  路由；没有 `routes` 键的对象与 `"routes": []` 仍是合法空路由配置，
  合法请求对其解析得到 `route_not_found`。`routes` 数组的每个元素必须
  是对象，null 也按元素类型错误处理（不报缺少 id），reason 指出从 1
  开始的路由序号、要求的对象类型和实际收到的类型，且即使请求只会命中
  较早的合法路由，后面的非对象元素也会使整份配置被拒绝。
  合法 JSON 中某条路由的 `id`、`methods`、`pathPrefix`、`upstream`
  字段类型本身不符（如 `methods` 写成字符串、数组元素不是字符串）时，
  reason 直接指出从 1 开始的路由序号与字段，而非把整份配置说成无效
  JSON；该路由同时提供了合法非空字符串 `id` 时附带该 id（即使它写在
  出错字段之后），但 `id` 自身类型错误时只报位置与字段。只有 JSON
  语法损坏才报解析失败（即使开头包含 `routes` 或完整的第一条路由），
  且不猜测出错字段或路由位置；配置结构错误与请求错误同时存在时先报告
  `invalid_config`。此外，`upstream` 用方括号包围主机时，括号内必须是合法
  IPv6 地址（完整写法、压缩写法、含 IPv4 尾段均可），允许带端口、用户信息
  与区域标识（`%25eth0`）；空括号、括号内为普通名称或 IPv4 地址（如
  `[not-an-ip]`、`[127.0.0.1]`）及格式错误的 IPv6 地址都使整份配置返回
  `invalid_config`，reason 指出从 1 开始的路由序号、id 与 `upstream` 字段，
  说明括号中的主机不是合法 IPv6 地址，而不是把配置 JSON 说成语法损坏；普通
  域名与不带方括号的 IPv4 主机不受影响。反过来，IPv6 字面量主机必须完整放
  在一对方括号内，端口写在括号之外（如 `http://[2001:db8::1]:8080/base`）：
  完整写法、压缩写法、含 IPv4 尾段及带 `%25eth0` 区域标识的地址，不加括号都
  被拒绝，`http://2001:db8::1/base`、`http://::1:8080/base` 与
  `http://::ffff:192.0.2.1/base` 均属此类，末尾是数字也不能使其成为合法配置
  （主机与端口边界有歧义时不猜测端口，也不自动补括号），带端口或用户信息的
  写法同样拒绝；reason 指出从 1 开始的路由序号、该路由 id 与 `upstream` 字段，
  说明 IPv6 主机缺少方括号，这是地址内容错误而非配置 JSON 语法损坏，且只检查
  主机段——用户信息或基础路径中出现冒号不影响判定。此外，每个上游都必须真正
  填写非空主机：`http://:8080/base`、`https://:8443`、`http://:/base` 都使
  整份配置返回 `invalid_config`，即使主机位置前带有用户名或密码（如
  `https://user:p%40ss@:8443/v1`）也相同——用户信息、端口和基础路径都不能
  补足缺失的主机，也不会补上任何默认地址；判断的是主机有没有填写，端口格式
  仍沿用现有规则，所以有主机的 `http://api.internal:/base`（空端口）继续按
  现有行为接受。reason 指出从 1 开始的路由序号、该路由 id 与 `upstream`
  字段，并说明上游缺少主机，既不能说成配置 JSON 解析失败，也不能说成 IPv6
  缺少方括号；配置中只要有一条路由存在此问题，即使当前请求只会命中较早的
  合法路由，整份配置也在读取时被拒绝。
- `invalid_request`：方法缺失或不合法、`target` 不以 `/` 开头、含片段、非法百分号转义，
  或直接出现不允许的字符（ASCII 空格、U+0000 至 U+001F 控制字符、U+007F，无论位于路径、
  参数名称还是参数值）。该字符检查在路由选择与查询串改写之前进行：没有路由命中、路由冲突，
  或 `remove`、`set` 会删除/覆盖携带该字符的参数时，仍返回 `invalid_request`；reason 指出
  target 含有不允许直接出现的字符，并以 U+XXXX 形式说明最先出现的那个字符（JSON 中的
  `\n`、`\t`、`\u0000` 等转义解码后按此规则处理）。百分号编码与直接字符严格区分：
  `/api/orders%20next` 与 `/api/orders?note=%0A%09` 继续按现有规则解析，路径中的编码不先
  解码再匹配，未改写的编码、参数顺序与空格写法保持原样，不删除控制字符后继续解析；中文等
  未涉及该规则的内容保持现有行为。
  只有 JSON 语法损坏才报解析失败，且不猜测哪个字段出错；合法 JSON 但最外层是
  数组、数字、字符串、布尔值或 null 时，reason 说明请求必须是 JSON 对象；合法
  对象中 `method` 或 `target` 写成数字、布尔值、对象、数组或 null 时，reason
  指出该字段必须是字符串并说明收到的类型（null 算类型错误，不是字段未填写），
  两个字段都出错时先报告 `method`，与字段书写顺序无关；空字符串仍是内容问题
  （方法必填、目标路径必须以 `/` 开头），不归为类型错误。
- `route_conflict` / `route_not_found`：见上。


## 技术方向

smart-contract-audit, formal-verification, symbolic-execution, fuzzing, security, exploit-analysis, reentrancy

## 运行要求

Go 1.26，仅使用标准库，全部行为可在本机 CPU 上离线复现。

1	// Offline route resolution: match a request against configured route prefixes
2	// and join the remainder onto the upstream base path without any network I/O.
3	package contractsentinel
4	
5	import (
6		"bytes"
7		"encoding/json"
8		"fmt"
9		"net/netip"
10		"net/url"
11		"sort"
12		"strings"
13	)
14	
15	// Route is one configured route: an id, accepted methods, a path prefix and
16	// the upstream URL requests on that route are forwarded to. An optional
17	// queryTransforms list rewrites the request query string after the route has
18	// been selected.
19	//
20	// QueryTransforms stays tag-less in the default (un)marshal sense: reading
21	// goes through Config.UnmarshalJSON, which decodes each route through the
22	// routeJSON raw mirror and validates the rules before they reach this field,
23	// and writing goes through Route.MarshalJSON, so the rules round-trip
24	// instead of being silently dropped (a plain json:"-" tag only omitted them
25	// on save).
26	type Route struct {
27		ID         string
28		Methods    []string
29		PathPrefix string
30		Upstream   string
31	
32		// QueryTransforms holds the validated rules. When it carries no rules
33		// the field is omitted on save, whether the source named no field or an
34		// explicit queryTransforms: [] — both are valid ways to write a route
35		// without rules, and ParseConfig accepts either.
36		QueryTransforms []*QueryTransform
37	}
38	
39	// pendingRoute is the read-side intermediate form of one route: the decoded
40	// basic fields alongside the still-unchecked raw queryTransforms value. It
41	// exists only inside the config reader, where the rules are validated against
42	// the route's 1-based position in check layer 3, and never becomes part of a
43	// finished Config — Route itself only ever carries the validated result, so
44	// no read path can observe a route that still holds unchecked rule text.
45	type pendingRoute struct {
46		route Route
47		// rawTransforms is the undecoded queryTransforms value, kept apart from
48		// the formal route data until checkQueryTransforms validates it.
49		rawTransforms json.RawMessage
50	}
51	
52	// MarshalJSON writes routes back in the shape ParseConfig accepts: the four
53	// basic fields in their canonical order, followed by queryTransforms when the
54	// route carries rules. A route without rules — whether the source omitted the
55	// field or named queryTransforms: [] — omits it, and ParseConfig accepts
56	// either spelling; the field is never written as null. The rules' order and
57	// literal strings are preserved byte for byte apart from JSON string
58	// escaping, so re-parsing the output and resolving yields the same routeId
59	// and upstreamURL.
60	func (r Route) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
61		type routeOut struct {
62			ID              string            `json:"id"`
63			Methods         []string          `json:"methods"`
64			PathPrefix      string            `json:"pathPrefix"`
65			Upstream        string            `json:"upstream"`
66			QueryTransforms []*QueryTransform `json:"queryTransforms,omitempty"`
67		}
68		return json.Marshal(routeOut{
69			ID:              r.ID,
70			Methods:         r.Methods,
71			PathPrefix:      r.PathPrefix,
72			Upstream:        r.Upstream,
73			QueryTransforms: r.QueryTransforms,
74		})
75	}
76	
77	// QueryTransform is one rule in a route's queryTransforms array: op is
78	// "set", "remove" or "rename"; name is matched against decoded parameter
79	// names, value (set only) is used literally, and to (rename only) is the
80	// literal replacement name.
81	type QueryTransform struct {
82		Op    string `json:"op"`
83		Name  string `json:"name"`
84		Value string `json:"value"`
85		To    string `json:"to"`
86	}
87	
88	// MarshalJSON renders each rule so the output satisfies the same constraints
89	// parseQueryTransforms enforces on input:
90	//   - set keeps "value" as a JSON string, including the empty string;
91	//   - remove emits only op and name (never value or to);
92	//   - rename keeps a non-empty "to" and never emits value.
93	//
94	// name, value and to are written as the literal strings read in — spaces,
95	// non-ASCII letters, '+' and '%' included — with only JSON string escaping,
96	// never query-string percent-encoding or decoding, so a re-read matches the
97	// same parameter names and applies the same literal values.
98	func (q *QueryTransform) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
99		switch q.Op {
100		case "set":
101			return json.Marshal(struct {
102				Op    string `json:"op"`
103				Name  string `json:"name"`
104				Value string `json:"value"`
105			}{q.Op, q.Name, q.Value})
106		case "rename":
107			return json.Marshal(struct {
108				Op   string `json:"op"`
109				Name string `json:"name"`
110				To   string `json:"to"`
111			}{q.Op, q.Name, q.To})
112		default:
113			// remove (and any op a validated config could never carry) writes
114			// neither value nor to, so the output cannot gain fields the reader
115			// rejects.
116			return json.Marshal(struct {
117				Op   string `json:"op"`
118				Name string `json:"name"`
119			}{q.Op, q.Name})
120		}
121	}
122	
123	// routeJSON mirrors Route but keeps every field raw: the basic fields are
124	// type-checked by decodeRoute with the route's position (and, when available,
125	// its id), so a wrong field type is reported on that route rather than as a
126	// generic JSON decode error, and queryTransforms can surface null, wrong
127	// types and malformed rules the same way.
128	type routeJSON struct {
129		ID              json.RawMessage `json:"id"`
130		Methods         json.RawMessage `json:"methods"`
131		PathPrefix      json.RawMessage `json:"pathPrefix"`
132		Upstream        json.RawMessage `json:"upstream"`
133		QueryTransforms json.RawMessage `json:"queryTransforms"`
134	}
135	
136	// decodeRoute type-checks and decodes one raw route object into its
137	// intermediate form: the basic fields land on the pending route, while the
138	// raw queryTransforms value travels alongside it, still unchecked, for check
139	// layer 3. loc is the route's 1-based location in its config (e.g.
140	// "route 2"). The element's JSON type is checked first: a null entry or any
141	// non-object value fails on the entry itself, naming the position, the
142	// required object type and the type actually received, instead of falling
143	// through to a missing-field error such as a missing id. Field type errors
144	// then carry that location and, when the route supplies a valid non-empty
145	// string id anywhere in its object (even after the offending field), that id.
146	// Missing fields stay silent here and are rejected later by validate, which
147	// preserves the existing missing-field behavior.
148	func decodeRoute(data []byte, loc string) (pendingRoute, *Failure) {
149		elem := bytes.TrimSpace(data)
150		if len(elem) == 0 || elem[0] != '{' {
151			return pendingRoute{}, failuref("invalid_config",
152				"%s: route entry must be an object, got %s", loc, jsonTypeName(elem))
153		}
154		var rj routeJSON
155		if err := json.Unmarshal(elem, &rj); err != nil {
156			// The element already parsed as one JSON value and starts with '{';
157			// an object that cannot be read is a syntax failure rather than a
158			// field type error.
159			return pendingRoute{}, failuref("invalid_config", "config is not valid JSON: %v", err)
160		}
161	
162		var pending pendingRoute
163		route := &pending.route
164		// Type-check id first so it can identify the route on an error in any
165		// later field regardless of object order. Only a valid non-empty JSON
166		// string becomes the label; a wrong-typed id is reported against the id
167		// field and never rendered (e.g. as a number or object) as the route's
168		// identity, so that error is located by position alone.
169		if !decodeStringField(rj.ID, &route.ID) {
170			return pendingRoute{}, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: id must be a string", loc)
171		}
172		label := loc
173		if route.ID != "" {
174			label = routeLabel(loc, route.ID)
175		}
176	
177		if f := decodeMethodsField(rj.Methods, label, &route.Methods); f != nil {
178			return pendingRoute{}, f
179		}
180		if f := decodeRouteStringField(rj.PathPrefix, label, "pathPrefix", &route.PathPrefix); f != nil {
181			return pendingRoute{}, f
182		}
183		if f := decodeRouteStringField(rj.Upstream, label, "upstream", &route.Upstream); f != nil {
184			return pendingRoute{}, f
185		}
186		pending.rawTransforms = rj.QueryTransforms
187		return pending, nil
188	}
189	
190	// decodeRouteStringField renders a route field's string type error with the
191	// route's position (and, when available, its id); the type decision itself is
192	// the shared decodeStringField. An absent field stays silent for the later
193	// required-field validation.
194	func decodeRouteStringField(raw json.RawMessage, label, field string, dst *string) *Failure {
195		if !decodeStringField(raw, dst) {
196			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s: %s must be a string", label, field)
197		}
198		return nil
199	}
200	
201	// decodeStringField type-checks a raw field that must hold a string. It is
202	// the one shared string-field decision used by both config and request
203	// decoding, so the absent / null / non-string / empty-string distinctions
204	// live in one place. It returns false only when the key is present with a
205	// non-string value (null included), which is always a field type error. An
206	// absent key leaves dst untouched, and a present string — the empty string
207	// included — is decoded into dst, so both reach the existing content checks
208	// unchanged.
209	func decodeStringField(raw json.RawMessage, dst *string) (isString bool) {
210		if len(raw) == 0 {
211			return true
212		}
213		return jsonString(raw, dst)
214	}
215	
216	// decodeMethodsField type-checks methods: it must be an array of strings
217	// when present. An absent field is left nil for later required-field
218	// validation; null or any non-array value fails the field, and a number,
219	// boolean, object or null entry fails with the offending entry's position.
220	func decodeMethodsField(raw json.RawMessage, label string, dst *[]string) *Failure {
221		if len(raw) == 0 {
222			return nil
223		}
224		body := bytes.TrimSpace(raw)
225		if string(body) == "null" || len(body) == 0 || body[0] != '[' {
226			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s: methods must be an array of strings", label)
227		}
228		var elems []json.RawMessage
229		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &elems); err != nil {
230			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s: methods must be an array of strings", label)
231		}
232		methods := make([]string, 0, len(elems))
233		for i, elem := range elems {
234			var m string
235			if !jsonString(bytes.TrimSpace(elem), &m) {
236				return failuref("invalid_config", "%s: methods entry %d must be a string", label, i+1)
237			}
238			methods = append(methods, m)
239		}
240		*dst = methods
241		return nil
242	}

244	// parseQueryTransforms decodes and validates the raw queryTransforms array
245	// of one route. loc identifies the route; rule errors additionally carry a
246	// 1-based rule index.
247	func parseQueryTransforms(raw json.RawMessage, loc, id string) ([]*QueryTransform, *Failure) {
248		body := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
249		if body == "null" {
250			return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: queryTransforms must not be null", routeLabel(loc, id))
251		}
252		var elems []json.RawMessage
253		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(body), &elems); err != nil {
254			return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: queryTransforms must be an array", routeLabel(loc, id))
255		}
256		transforms := make([]*QueryTransform, 0, len(elems))
257		for i, elem := range elems {
258			ruleLoc := fmt.Sprintf("%s, queryTransforms rule %d", routeLabel(loc, id), i+1)
259			if string(bytes.TrimSpace(elem)) == "null" {
260				return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: rule must not be null", ruleLoc)
261			}
262			var fields map[string]json.RawMessage
263			if err := json.Unmarshal(elem, &fields); err != nil {
264				return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: rule must be a JSON object", ruleLoc)
265			}
266	
267			qt := &QueryTransform{}
268			opRaw, ok := fields["op"]
269			switch {
270			case !ok:
271				return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: op is required", ruleLoc)
272			case !jsonString(opRaw, &qt.Op):
273				return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: op must be a string", ruleLoc)
274			case qt.Op != "set" && qt.Op != "remove" && qt.Op != "rename":
275				return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: unknown op %q (only set, remove and rename are supported)", ruleLoc, qt.Op)
276			}
277	
278			nameRaw, ok := fields["name"]
279			switch {
280			case !ok:
281				return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: name is required", ruleLoc)
282			case !jsonString(nameRaw, &qt.Name):
283				return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: name must be a non-empty string", ruleLoc)
284			case qt.Name == "":
285				return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: name must be a non-empty string", ruleLoc)
286			}
287	
288			valueRaw, hasValue := fields["value"]
289			toRaw, hasTo := fields["to"]
290			switch qt.Op {
291			case "set":
292				if !hasValue {
293					return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: set requires a string value", ruleLoc)
294				}
295				if !jsonString(valueRaw, &qt.Value) {
296					return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: value must be a string", ruleLoc)
297				}
298			case "remove":
299				if hasValue {
300					return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: remove must not include a value", ruleLoc)
301				}
302			case "rename":
303				if hasValue {
304					return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: rename must not include a value", ruleLoc)
305				}
306				switch {
307				case !hasTo:
308					return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: rename requires a non-empty string to", ruleLoc)
309				case !jsonString(toRaw, &qt.To):
310					return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: to must be a non-empty string", ruleLoc)
311				case qt.To == "":
312					return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "%s: to must be a non-empty string", ruleLoc)
313				}
314			}
315			transforms = append(transforms, qt)
316		}
317		return transforms, nil
318	}

320	// jsonString decodes raw into s and reports whether raw is a JSON string
321	// (null, numbers, objects and arrays fail).
322	func jsonString(raw json.RawMessage, s *string) bool {
323		if len(raw) == 0 || raw[0] != '"' {
324			return false
325		}
326		return json.Unmarshal(raw, s) == nil
327	}

329	// routeLabel renders the human-readable route location, adding the id when
330	// the configuration supplied one.
331	func routeLabel(loc, id string) string {
332		if id != "" {
333			return fmt.Sprintf("%s (id %q)", loc, id)
334		}
335		return loc
336	}

338	// Config is the resolve configuration: a flat array of routes.
339	type Config struct {
340		Routes []Route `json:"routes"`
341	}
342	
343	// MarshalJSON writes the config back in the shape ParseConfig accepts. A
344	// non-nil empty (or nil) routes slice is emitted as "routes": [] rather than
345	// "routes": null, which ParseConfig would reject with invalid_config; the
346	// routes keep their parsed order and each route marshals through
347	// Route.MarshalJSON so its queryTransforms survive the save.
348	func (cfg *Config) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
349		routes := cfg.Routes
350		if routes == nil {
351			routes = []Route{}
352		}
353		return json.Marshal(struct {
354			Routes []Route `json:"routes"`
355		}{Routes: routes})
356	}
357	
358	// UnmarshalJSON runs check layers 1–3 of config reading (see ParseConfig for
359	// the full layer list and the error-selection rules): JSON syntax, then the
360	// document structure and basic field types, then the queryTransforms rules.
361	// Layer 4 (field contents) is Config.validate, run by ParseConfig after
362	// decoding. The routes are decoded one entry at a time from raw values, each
363	// type-checked against its 1-based position in this config, so a wrong field
364	// type is reported on the offending route (with its id when available)
365	// instead of as a generic JSON syntax failure, and configs parsed
366	// concurrently or interleaved in the same process cannot shift each other's
367	// route numbering. A broken JSON document fails the outer decode and is
368	// reported as a parse failure, without a guessed route position or field.
369	func (cfg *Config) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
370		read, err := readConfig(data)
371		if err != nil {
372			return err
373		}
374		*cfg = *read
375		return nil
376	}
377	
378	// readConfig runs check layers 1–3 and returns the configuration with every
379	// route's basic fields decoded and its queryTransforms validated. The
380	// intermediate pendingRoutes keep the unchecked rule text out of the
381	// returned Config; layer 4 (field contents) is Config.validate, run by
382	// ParseConfig.
383	func readConfig(data []byte) (*Config, error) {
384		// Layer 1: JSON syntax. A broken document is only ever a parse failure,
385		// reported without a guessed route position or field.
386		body, err := unmarshalJSONValue(data)
387		if err != nil {
388			return nil, err
389		}
390		// Layer 2: structure and basic field types.
391		if f := requireJSONObject(body, "invalid_config", "config", true); f != nil {
392			return nil, f
393		}
394		routes, err := decodeConfigRoutes(body)
395		if err != nil {
396			return nil, err
397		}
398		// Layer 3: query rewrite rules, checked only once every route's basic
399		// fields have the right type, so a type error on any route — earlier or
400		// later — is always reported before any rule error.
401		if f := checkQueryTransforms(routes); f != nil {
402			return nil, f
403		}
404		cfg := &Config{Routes: make([]Route, len(routes))}
405		for i := range routes {
406			cfg.Routes[i] = routes[i].route
407		}
408		return cfg, nil
409	}
410	
411	// decodeConfigRoutes is check layer 2: the top-level object is taken apart
412	// and every route entry is type-checked against its 1-based position. The
413	// routes field must hold an array when present — null is a type error here,
414	// never an absent field: a config that explicitly supplies routes must supply
415	// an array. A non-object entry (null included) fails on that entry before
416	// any field is inspected, and a wrong field type is reported on the offending
417	// route with its id when the route supplies a valid non-empty string id
418	// anywhere in its object. Each route's unchecked queryTransforms value
419	// travels in the returned pendingRoutes for layer 3.
420	func decodeConfigRoutes(body json.RawMessage) ([]pendingRoute, error) {
421		var fields map[string]json.RawMessage
422		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &fields); err != nil {
423			return nil, err
424		}
425	
426		var rawRoutes []json.RawMessage
427		if raw, ok := fields["routes"]; ok {
428			elem := bytes.TrimSpace(raw)
429			if len(elem) == 0 || elem[0] != '[' {
430				return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "routes must be an array, got %s", jsonTypeName(elem))
431			}
432			if err := json.Unmarshal(elem, &rawRoutes); err != nil {
433				return nil, err
434			}
435		}
436	
437		routes := make([]pendingRoute, len(rawRoutes))
438		for i, entry := range rawRoutes {
439			route, f := decodeRoute(entry, fmt.Sprintf("route %d", i+1))
440			if f != nil {
441				return nil, f
442			}
443			routes[i] = route
444		}
445		return routes, nil
446	}
447	
448	// checkQueryTransforms is check layer 3: every route's raw queryTransforms
449	// value is decoded and validated against the route's 1-based position, in
450	// routes-array order, and the validated rules replace the pending raw value.
451	// It runs only after layer 2 has cleared every route, so a basic-field type
452	// error on any route — earlier or later — is always reported before any rule
453	// error, while within this layer the earliest route (and within it the
454	// earliest rule) wins.
455	func checkQueryTransforms(routes []pendingRoute) *Failure {
456		for i := range routes {
457			if len(routes[i].rawTransforms) == 0 {
458				continue // field absent
459			}
460			loc := fmt.Sprintf("route %d", i+1)
461			transforms, f := parseQueryTransforms(routes[i].rawTransforms, loc, routes[i].route.ID)
462			if f != nil {
463				return f
464			}
465			routes[i].route.QueryTransforms = transforms
466			routes[i].rawTransforms = nil
467		}
468		return nil
469	}
470	
471	// unmarshalJSONValue is the shared first step of parsing either input: it
472	// confirms the document is one syntactically valid JSON value, without
473	// judging its shape. It returns encoding/json's own error verbatim, so each
474	// caller keeps its existing handling (ParseConfig wraps a returned error just
475	// as Config.UnmarshalJSON returning it directly always has).
476	func unmarshalJSONValue(data []byte) (json.RawMessage, error) {
477		var doc json.RawMessage
478		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &doc); err != nil {
479			return nil, err
480		}
481		return bytes.TrimSpace(doc), nil
482	}
483	
484	// requireJSONObject is the shared top-level shape check: a syntactically
485	// legal value that is not a JSON object is a structural error in the caller's
486	// code saying "<what> must be a JSON object", never a parse failure and never
487	// a guessed field or route position. Config errors additionally name the type
488	// actually received ("got <type>"); the request wording omits it.
489	func requireJSONObject(doc json.RawMessage, code, what string, nameType bool) *Failure {
490		if len(doc) == 0 || doc[0] != '{' {
491			if nameType {
492				return failuref(code, "%s must be a JSON object, got %s", what, jsonTypeName(doc))
493			}
494			return failuref(code, "%s must be a JSON object", what)
495		}
496		return nil
497	}

499	// Request is one resolution request: an HTTP method and a request target
500	// (path with an optional raw query string).
501	type Request struct {
502		Method string `json:"method"`
503		Target string `json:"target"`
504	}
505	
506	// Resolution is the successful result of matching a request.
507	type Resolution struct {
508		RouteID     string `json:"routeId"`
509		UpstreamURL string `json:"upstreamURL"`
510	}
511	
512	// Failure carries a stable machine-readable code and a human-readable reason.
513	type Failure struct {
514		Code       string   `json:"code"`
515		Reason     string   `json:"reason"`
516		Candidates []string `json:"candidates,omitempty"`
517	}
518	
519	func (f *Failure) Error() string { return f.Code + ": " + f.Reason }
520	
521	func failuref(code, format string, args ...any) *Failure {
522		return &Failure{Code: code, Reason: fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)}
523	}

525	// ParseConfig parses and fully validates the route configuration. Reading
526	// checks the document in four layers, and the first layer that finds a
527	// problem decides which error is reported:
528	//
529	//  1. JSON syntax: a broken document is only ever a parse failure, reported
530	//     without a guessed route position or field.
531	//  2. Structure and basic field types: the top-level value must be an
532	//     object, routes must be an array of objects, and id, methods,
533	//     pathPrefix and upstream must carry their JSON types.
534	//  3. Query rewrite rules: each route's queryTransforms array and every rule
535	//     in it.
536	//  4. Field contents: a non-empty unique id, legal methods, an absolute
537	//     pathPrefix and a valid upstream (Config.validate).
538	//
539	// Within one layer the earliest array position wins — routes by their
540	// position in the routes array and rules by their position in the route's
541	// queryTransforms array, never by id ordering or by the object field order.
542	// Layers 1–3 run in Config.UnmarshalJSON (so they also guard a plain
543	// json.Unmarshal into a Config); layer 4 runs here, after decoding. Every
544	// failure hands back no config at all, so a half-parsed configuration can
545	// never resolve a request.
546	func ParseConfig(data []byte) (*Config, *Failure) {
547		var cfg Config
548		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &cfg); err != nil {
549			if f, ok := err.(*Failure); ok {
550				return nil, f
551			}
552			return nil, failuref("invalid_config", "config is not valid JSON: %v", err)
553		}
554		if f := cfg.validate(); f != nil {
555			return nil, f
556		}
557		return &cfg, nil
558	}
559	
560	// validate is check layer 4 (see ParseConfig): the field contents of every
561	// route, in routes-array order. It runs only after layers 1–3 have cleared
562	// the whole document, so any structure, field-type or rule error anywhere is
563	// reported before any content error.
564	func (cfg *Config) validate() *Failure {
565		seenIDs := make(map[string]int, len(cfg.Routes))
566		for i := range cfg.Routes {
567			route := &cfg.Routes[i]
568			loc := fmt.Sprintf("route %d", i+1)
569			if route.ID == "" {
570				return failuref("invalid_config", "%s: id must be non-empty", loc)
571			}
572			if first, ok := seenIDs[route.ID]; ok {
573				return failuref("invalid_config", "%s: duplicate id %q (already used by route %d)", loc, route.ID, first)
574			}
575			seenIDs[route.ID] = i + 1
576	
577			if len(route.Methods) == 0 {
578				return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): methods must be a non-empty array", loc, route.ID)
579			}
580			for _, method := range route.Methods {
581				switch {
582				case method == "":
583					return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): methods must not contain empty entries", loc, route.ID)
584				case method == "*":
585					// Wildcard matching any legal method.
586				case !isToken(method):
587					return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): invalid method %q", loc, route.ID, method)
588				}
589			}
590	
591			if f := validatePrefix(route.PathPrefix, loc, route.ID); f != nil {
592				return f
593			}
594			if f := validateUpstream(route.Upstream, loc, route.ID); f != nil {
595				return f
596			}
597		}
598		return nil
599	}
600	
601	func validatePrefix(prefix, loc, id string) *Failure {
602		switch {
603		case prefix == "" || prefix[0] != '/':
604			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): pathPrefix must start with /", loc, id)
605		case prefix != "/" && strings.HasSuffix(prefix, "/"):
606			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): pathPrefix must not end with / except for root", loc, id)
607		case strings.ContainsAny(prefix, "?#"):
608			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): pathPrefix must not contain a query string or fragment", loc, id)
609		case !validPercentEscapes(prefix):
610			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): pathPrefix contains an invalid percent escape", loc, id)
611		}
612		return nil
613	}
614	
615	// upstreamParts is the one shared reading of a raw upstream URL's address
616	// boundaries. Every field is a slice of the original bytes (nothing is
617	// copied, decoded or normalized), so validation and joining cannot disagree
618	// about where one part ends and the next begins:
619	//
620	//	scheme "://" [userinfo "@"] hostPort basePath
621	//
622	// authority runs from after "://" to the first path slash, and hostPort is
623	// the authority after its last '@', so colons in userinfo or the base path
624	// can never be read as part of an IPv6 host, while brackets, a port and a
625	// zone stay inside hostPort.
626	type upstreamParts struct {
627		raw       string // the upstream exactly as configured; every other field slices this
628		schemeEnd int    // index of the ':' in "://", or -1 when the scheme is absent
629		authority string // bytes between "://" and the first path slash (userinfo included)
630		hostPort  string // authority after the last '@' (host plus optional port)
631		basePath  string // from the first path slash to the end, or ""
632	}
633	
634	// splitUpstream applies the single boundary rule shared by the bracketed-host
635	// check, the unbracketed-IPv6 check and the final join. It never rejects
636	// anything on its own: a raw value without "://" comes back with schemeEnd
637	// set to -1 and empty parts, leaving the generic absolute-URL check to
638	// report it, exactly as the per-caller preamble used to.
639	func splitUpstream(raw string) upstreamParts {
640		p := upstreamParts{raw: raw, schemeEnd: -1}
641		i := strings.Index(raw, "://")
642		if i < 0 {
643			return p
644		}
645		p.schemeEnd = i
646		tail := raw[i+3:]
647		if j := strings.IndexByte(tail, '/'); j >= 0 {
648			p.authority = tail[:j]
649			p.basePath = tail[j:]
650		} else {
651			p.authority = tail
652		}
653		// Any userinfo precedes the host and ends at the last '@'; that boundary
654		// is what keeps a userinfo colon out of the IPv6-host checks.
655		p.hostPort = p.authority
656		if k := strings.LastIndexByte(p.authority, '@'); k >= 0 {
657			p.hostPort = p.authority[k+1:]
658		}
659		return p
660	}
661	
662	func validateUpstream(raw, loc, id string) *Failure {
663		if strings.ContainsAny(raw, "?#") {
664			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): upstream must not contain a query string or fragment", loc, id)
665		}
666		// Validate the host's IP-literal spelling against the raw string before
667		// url.Parse: square brackets are the IP-literal marker, so whatever they
668		// enclose must be a legal IPv6 address (full, compressed or IPv4-tail,
669		// zone included) rather than a name or an IPv4 address, and an IPv6
670		// literal may never appear without that pair of brackets. Both checks and
671		// the later join read the same splitUpstream boundaries, which keeps the
672		// rules independent of url.Parse's parser strictness and lets the reason
673		// name the field and the actual problem instead of surfacing a generic URL
674		// parse error (an unbracketed literal otherwise reaches the user as a
675		// misleading "invalid port" complaint).
676		p := splitUpstream(raw)
677		if f := validateBracketedUpstreamHost(p, loc, id); f != nil {
678			return f
679		}
680		if f := validateUnbracketedUpstreamHost(p, loc, id); f != nil {
681			return f
682		}
683		if f := validateUpstreamHostPresent(p, loc, id); f != nil {
684			return f
685		}
686		if f := validateUpstreamBasePathSpace(p, loc, id); f != nil {
687			return f
688		}
689		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
690		if err != nil {
691			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): upstream is not a valid URL: %v", loc, id, err)
692		}
693		if u.Scheme != "http" && u.Scheme != "https" {
694			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): upstream must be an absolute http or https URL", loc, id)
695		}
696		if u.Host == "" {
697			return failuref("invalid_config", "%s (id %q): upstream must include a host", loc, id)
698		}
699		return nil
700	}
701	
702	// validateUpstreamHostPresent enforces on the split raw boundaries that the
703	// authority carries a non-empty host:
704	//
705	//	scheme "://" [userinfo "@"] host [":" port] [basePath]
706	//
707	// The check is needed because url.Parse treats a leading colon as a port
708	// separator with an empty hostname: it reads "http://:8080/base" with
709	// Host==":8080" and Hostname()=="" instead of rejecting it, so a check on
710	// u.Host alone lets the address through and the joined upstream is emitted
711	// without a host. The raw decision therefore fails every hostPort that is
712	// empty or begins with the port colon — an empty authority
713	// ("http:///base"), an authority reduced to userinfo ("http://u@/base"),
714	// a bare port with or without digits ("http://:8080/base",
715	// "https://:8443", "http://:/base") and any of those after userinfo
716	// ("https://user:p%40ss@:8443/v1"). Neither userinfo, the port nor a base
717	// path can fill the host slot, no default address is ever substituted, and
718	// a host that is simply followed by an empty port ("http://host:/base")
719	// stays accepted: its hostPort begins with the host, not the separator.
720	// Like the bracket rules this is a content error in a syntactically valid
721	// JSON document — the reason names the route's 1-based position, its id and
722	// the upstream field and says the upstream is missing a host, never that
723	// the JSON is broken or that an IPv6 literal needs brackets.
724	func validateUpstreamHostPresent(p upstreamParts, loc, id string) *Failure {
725		if p.schemeEnd < 0 {
726			return nil // no scheme: the generic absolute-URL check reports this
727		}
728		hostPort := p.hostPort
729		if hostPort != "" && hostPort[0] != ':' {
730			return nil
731		}
732		return failuref("invalid_config",
733			"%s: upstream %q is missing a host: the address must carry a non-empty host before any port (e.g. \"http://example.com:8080/base\"); a port cannot serve as the host, and userinfo or a base path cannot fill the host in either; no default host is added",
734			routeLabel(loc, id), p.raw)
735	}

737	// validateUpstreamBasePathSpace rejects a direct ASCII space (U+0020) in the
738	// upstream base path — inside a path segment, beside a slash or at the end,
739	// it is all the same error. Only percent encoding may carry a space there:
740	// "%20" is legal path content and is never decoded first, so an encoded
741	// space stays accepted while the literal byte is rejected. The check reads
742	// the same splitUpstream base-path boundaries the join uses, so a space that
743	// would reach upstreamURL can never pass validation. It is decided on the
744	// decoded configured string (a " " JSON escape decodes to the same
745	// byte), only the ASCII space is rejected — the rule is not widened to other
746	// Unicode whitespace — and the address is judged exactly as configured: the
747	// space is never stripped, the path never trimmed and the byte never
748	// re-encoded on the user's behalf. The reason names the route's 1-based
749	// position, its id and the upstream field; like the host rules this is a
750	// content error in a syntactically valid JSON document, never a JSON parse
751	// failure.
752	func validateUpstreamBasePathSpace(p upstreamParts, loc, id string) *Failure {
753		if p.schemeEnd < 0 {
754			return nil // no scheme: the generic absolute-URL check reports this
755		}
756		if !strings.ContainsRune(p.basePath, ' ') {
757			return nil
758		}
759		return failuref("invalid_config",
760			"%s: upstream base path contains an unencoded space (U+0020): a space in the upstream address must be percent-encoded as %%20 in the configuration; the address is used exactly as configured and the space is never stripped, the path never trimmed and the byte never encoded on its behalf",
761			routeLabel(loc, id))
762	}

764	// validateBracketedUpstreamHost checks the split raw upstream's authority for
765	// an IP literal in square brackets: brackets are reserved for an IPv6 (or
766	// future IP-version) literal, so their content must parse as an IPv6 address
767	// — full form, compressed form or an IPv6 address with an embedded IPv4
768	// tail — and the brackets must wrap the whole host exactly once:
769	//
770	//	"[" IPv6 "]" [ ":" *DIGIT ]
771	//
772	// A port, userinfo and a percent-encoded zone ("%25eth0") are allowed and
773	// never alter the literal's bytes; an empty pair of brackets, a plain
774	// hostname such as "[not-an-ip]", a bare IPv4 address such as
775	// "[127.0.0.1]", a malformed IPv6 literal, a missing closing bracket, a
776	// second bracket group such as "[::1][::2]", a stray closing bracket or any
777	// other text between the closing bracket and the start of the base path
778	// (including junk around the port such as "[::1]:80a" or "[::1]x]:80") are
779	// rejected — a legal first literal never legitimizes trailing content. The
780	// reason names the route, its id and the upstream field. This is a content
781	// error in a syntactically valid JSON document, never a JSON parse failure,
782	// and the rule is enforced here on the raw bytes rather than left to
783	// url.Parse's parser strictness.
784	func validateBracketedUpstreamHost(p upstreamParts, loc, id string) *Failure {
785		if p.schemeEnd < 0 {
786			return nil // no scheme: the generic absolute-URL check reports this
787		}
788		hostPort := p.hostPort
789	
790		if !strings.ContainsAny(hostPort, "[]") {
791			return nil // ordinary reg-name (domain) or bare IPv4 host stays as-is
792		}
793		label := routeLabel(loc, id)
794		if !strings.HasPrefix(hostPort, "[") {
795			return failuref("invalid_config",
796				"%s: upstream bracketed host must be a single '[' IPv6 address ']' pair: '[' may only open the host", label)
797		}
798		closeBracket := strings.IndexByte(hostPort, ']')
799		if closeBracket < 0 {
800			return failuref("invalid_config",
801				"%s: upstream bracketed host must be a valid IPv6 address but the closing ']' is missing", label)
802		}
803		literal := hostPort[1:closeBracket]
804		// The zone delimiter is percent-encoded in the URL ("%25"); decode the
805		// literal's escapes once so netip sees "fe80::1%eth0" while every other
806		// byte keeps its original spelling.
807		decoded, err := url.PathUnescape(literal)
808		if err != nil {
809			return invalidBracketedHost(label, literal)
810		}
811		addr, err := netip.ParseAddr(decoded)
812		if err != nil || !addr.Is6() {
813			// ParseAddr accepts a bare IPv4 address; brackets may only carry
814			// IPv6, so "[127.0.0.1]" is rejected even though it is a valid IP.
815			return invalidBracketedHost(label, literal)
816		}
817		// The one closing bracket ends the host: the rest of the authority may
818		// be empty or the optional port the generic parser already allows
819		// (":" followed by digits, an empty port included). A repeated bracket
820		// group, a stray ']', or any other text before, beside or after a port
821		// fails here even though the first literal was valid — the brackets
822		// must enclose the whole host exactly once.
823		suffix := hostPort[closeBracket+1:]
824		switch {
825		case suffix == "":
826			return nil
827		case strings.ContainsAny(suffix, "[]"):
828			return invalidBracketedHostShape(label, suffix)
829		case suffix[0] != ':':
830			return invalidBracketedHostShape(label, suffix)
831		}
832		port := suffix[1:]
833		for i := 0; i < len(port); i++ {
834			if port[i] < '0' || port[i] > '9' {
835				return invalidBracketedHostShape(label, suffix)
836			}
837		}
838		return nil
839	}

841	// invalidBracketedHost builds the content error for a bracketed host whose
842	// content is not a legal IPv6 literal.
843	func invalidBracketedHost(label, literal string) *Failure {
844		return failuref("invalid_config",
845			"%s: upstream host in brackets must be a valid IPv6 address, but %q is not a legal IPv6 address", label, literal)
846	}

848	// validateUnbracketedUpstreamHost checks the split raw upstream's
849	// authority-without-brackets (hostPort) against the authority grammar:
850	//
851	//	host = IP-literal / IPv4address / reg-name
852	//	IP-literal = "[" ( IPv6address / ... ) "]"
853	//
854	// An unbracketed host part may therefore carry at most one colon, the one
855	// separating the host from its port:
856	//
857	//	reg-name [ ":" port ]
858	//
859	// Two or more colons are illegal no matter what the bytes spell: a bare IPv6
860	// literal leaves the host/port boundary undefined (the reader cannot tell
861	// "::1" from "::1:8080" with a port) and must be written as "[2001:db8::1]",
862	// while a name such as "api:internal:8080" or even a malformed IPv6-shaped
863	// spelling such as "2001:db8:::1" is not rescued by a numeric last segment —
864	// an extra colon stays an extra colon whether or not the address parses as
865	// IPv6 and whether or not a base path follows. The spelling is rejected on
866	// the colon count alone: the host and port are never guessed apart, brackets
867	// are never inserted and a trailing run of digits is never promoted to a
868	// port, so validity never depends on this Go release's url.Parse port
869	// strictness.
870	//
871	// When the part does parse as an IPv6 literal as written, the reason keeps
872	// the existing missing-brackets wording; a part that is merely
873	// multi-colon gets the extra-colon wording. The decision never strips a
874	// trailing ":<digits>" segment as a hypothetical port: every true bare IPv6
875	// spelling already parses whole ("::1:8080" and "fe80::1:8443" are complete
876	// addresses, whose last hextet merely happens to be digits), so stripping
877	// would only mislabel a malformed spelling such as "2001:db8:::1" that
878	// parses once a hextet is removed. Both reasons cover every form — the full
879	// form, the compressed form ("::1"), an IPv6 address with an embedded IPv4
880	// tail ("::ffff:192.0.2.1") and a percent-encoded zone ("%25eth0") — and
881	// both name the route's 1-based position, its id and the upstream field.
882	//
883	// Ordinary domains and bare IPv4 hosts (with or without a port) stay
884	// untouched, and the colons in userinfo or the base path are never
885	// inspected: only hostPort — the authority after the last '@' and before
886	// the first '/' according to the shared splitUpstream boundaries — is
887	// considered. Like the bracketed-host rule this is a content error in a
888	// syntactically valid JSON document, never a JSON parse failure, and it is
889	// decided on the raw bytes before url.Parse so the wording cannot regress to
890	// that parser's generic "invalid port" error.
891	func validateUnbracketedUpstreamHost(p upstreamParts, loc, id string) *Failure {
892		if p.schemeEnd < 0 {
893			return nil // no scheme: the generic absolute-URL check reports this
894		}
895		hostPort := p.hostPort
896		if hostPort == "" || strings.ContainsAny(hostPort, "[]") {
897			// No host (the generic check reports it) or a bracketed literal,
898			// which the bracketed-host validator owns.
899			return nil
900		}
901	
902		// A single colon is the legal host/port separator ("host:8080"); zero
903		// colons is a bare host. Count raw colons only: percent-encoded colons
904		// ("%3A") carry no separator byte, and userinfo and the base path were
905		// sliced off by splitUpstream.
906		if strings.Count(hostPort, ":") <= 1 {
907			return nil
908		}
909		label := routeLabel(loc, id)
910	
911		// Classify the spelling as written, never guessing a host/port split:
912		// percent-decode once so a "%25eth0" zone reaches netip as "%eth0" while
913		// every other byte keeps its spelling, then parse the whole hostPort. A
914		// legal IPv6 literal keeps the existing missing-brackets reason (this
915		// covers every form, "::1:8080" and "fe80::1:8443" included — a trailing
916		// hextet of digits is part of the address, not a guessed port); anything
917		// else that merely carries extra colons gets the extra-colon reason.
918		decoded, err := url.PathUnescape(hostPort)
919		if err == nil {
920			if addr, perr := netip.ParseAddr(decoded); perr == nil && addr.Is6() {
921				return failuref("invalid_config",
922					"%s: upstream IPv6 host %q is missing its square brackets: an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in a pair of brackets with any port outside them (e.g. \"[2001:db8::1]:8080\"); brackets are never added and a trailing number is not guessed as a port",
923					label, hostPort)
924			}
925		}
926		return failuref("invalid_config",
927			"%s: upstream %q has an unbracketed host part %q with more than one colon: a host without square brackets may contain at most the one colon separating it from its port (e.g. \"example.com:8080\"); an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets (e.g. \"[2001:db8::1]:8080\") and the host and port are never guessed apart",
928			label, p.raw, hostPort)
929	}

931	// invalidBracketedHostShape builds the content error for a bracketed host
932	// whose trailing bytes break the "single '[' IPv6 ']' pair plus optional
933	// port" grammar, e.g. a repeated bracket group, a stray closing bracket or
934	// non-port text after the closing bracket.
935	func invalidBracketedHostShape(label, suffix string) *Failure {
936		return failuref("invalid_config",
937			"%s: upstream bracketed host must be a single '[' IPv6 address ']' pair followed only by an optional port, but %q follows the closing ']'", label, suffix)
938	}

940	// requestJSON mirrors Request but keeps method and target raw, so a valid
941	// JSON document whose fields merely have the wrong JSON type is reported on
942	// the offending field instead of as a generic JSON decode error.
943	type requestJSON struct {
944		Method json.RawMessage `json:"method"`
945		Target json.RawMessage `json:"target"`
946	}

948	// ParseRequest parses and validates one JSON request. Three failure shapes are
949	// kept apart: a document whose JSON syntax is broken fails as a parse failure
950	// without guessing a field; a syntactically valid non-object document (array,
951	// number, string, boolean or null) must be a JSON object; a valid object whose
952	// method or target is not a string fails on that field, naming the JSON type
953	// actually received (null counts as a type error, never as a missing field).
954	// method is always checked before target, regardless of the key order in the
955	// object. Only after both fields are present strings are their contents
956	// (required method, legal token, absolute target without a fragment, a bad
957	// percent escape, or a direct space/control character) validated, so an empty
958	// string stays a content error.
959	func ParseRequest(data []byte) (*Request, *Failure) {
960		body, err := unmarshalJSONValue(data)
961		if err != nil {
962			return nil, failuref("invalid_request", "request is not valid JSON: %v", err)
963		}
964		if f := requireJSONObject(body, "invalid_request", "request", false); f != nil {
965			return nil, f
966		}
967	
968		var rj requestJSON
969		if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &rj); err != nil {
970			// The document already parsed as one JSON value and starts with '{';
971			// keep this as a parse failure rather than a field error if the object
972			// itself cannot be read.
973			return nil, failuref("invalid_request", "request is not valid JSON: %v", err)
974		}
975	
976		var req Request
977		// method is always checked before target, regardless of the key order in
978		// the object; the absent/null/non-string distinction is the shared
979		// decodeStringField, so only the request wording is added here.
980		if f := decodeRequestStringField(rj.Method, "method", &req.Method); f != nil {
981			return nil, f
982		}
983		if f := decodeRequestStringField(rj.Target, "target", &req.Target); f != nil {
984			return nil, f
985		}
986	
987		switch {
988		case req.Method == "":
989			return nil, failuref("invalid_request", "method is required")
990		case !isToken(req.Method):
991			return nil, failuref("invalid_request", "method %q is not a legal HTTP method", req.Method)
992		}
993		switch {
994		case req.Target == "" || req.Target[0] != '/':
995			return nil, failuref("invalid_request", "target must start with /")
996		case strings.Contains(req.Target, "#"):
997			return nil, failuref("invalid_request", "target must not contain a fragment")
998		case !validPercentEscapes(req.Target):
999			return nil, failuref("invalid_request", "target contains an invalid percent escape")
1000		}
1001		if f := validateTargetCharacters(req.Target); f != nil {
1002			return nil, f
1003		}
1004		return &req, nil
1005	}

1007	// decodeRequestStringField renders the request wording for one string field;
1008	// the absent/null/non-string decision itself is the shared
1009	// decodeStringField. An absent field (no such key) is left as the zero value
1010	// so the later content checks keep their "field is required" behavior; null
1011	// or any non-string JSON value is a type error that names the field and the
1012	// JSON type that was actually supplied.
1013	func decodeRequestStringField(raw json.RawMessage, field string, dst *string) *Failure {
1014		if !decodeStringField(raw, dst) {
1015			return failuref("invalid_request", "%s must be a string, got %s", field, jsonTypeName(raw))
1016		}
1017		return nil
1018	}

1020	// jsonTypeName names the JSON type of a syntactically valid raw value, in the
1021	// terms the request error reasons use: "null", "a boolean", "a number",
1022	// "a string", "an array" or "an object".
1023	func jsonTypeName(raw json.RawMessage) string {
1024		switch bytes.TrimSpace(raw)[0] {
1025		case 'n':
1026			return "null"
1027		case 't', 'f':
1028			return "a boolean"
1029		case '"':
1030			return "a string"
1031		case '[':
1032			return "an array"
1033		case '{':
1034			return "an object"
1035		default:
1036			return "a number"
1037		}
1038	}

1040	// Resolve matches a validated request against a validated configuration and
1041	// computes the upstream URL. Failure codes are route_not_found and
1042	// route_conflict.
1043	func Resolve(cfg *Config, req *Request) (*Resolution, *Failure) {
1044		// Reject a target carrying a direct space or control character before
1045		// route selection, conflict resolution and query rewriting, so such a
1046		// request can never match a prefix (and carry the byte into
1047		// upstreamURL), report a conflict, or have a remove/set hide the
1048		// offending parameter. ParseRequest already ran this check; it is
1049		// repeated here so a request built in-process cannot bypass it.
1050		if f := validateTargetCharacters(req.Target); f != nil {
1051			return nil, f
1052		}
1053		path := req.Target
1054		if i := strings.IndexByte(path, '?'); i >= 0 {
1055			path = path[:i]
1056		}
1057	
1058		type candidate struct {
1059			route    *Route
1060			concrete bool
1061		}
1062		var matched []candidate
1063		for i := range cfg.Routes {
1064			route := &cfg.Routes[i]
1065			concrete, wildcard := methodMatch(route.Methods, req.Method)
1066			if !concrete && !wildcard {
1067				continue
1068			}
1069			if !prefixMatch(route.PathPrefix, path) {
1070				continue
1071			}
1072			matched = append(matched, candidate{route, concrete})
1073		}
1074		if len(matched) == 0 {
1075			return nil, failuref("route_not_found", "no route matches %s %s", req.Method, path)
1076		}
1077	
1078		// Longest prefix wins.
1079		bestLen := 0
1080		for _, c := range matched {
1081			if n := len(c.route.PathPrefix); n > bestLen {
1082				bestLen = n
1083			}
1084		}
1085		winners := matched[:0]
1086		for _, c := range matched {
1087			if len(c.route.PathPrefix) == bestLen {
1088				winners = append(winners, c)
1089			}
1090		}
1091	
1092		// Among equal prefixes a concrete method beats the wildcard.
1093		var concrete []candidate
1094		for _, c := range winners {
1095			if c.concrete {
1096				concrete = append(concrete, c)
1097			}
1098		}
1099		if len(concrete) > 0 {
1100			winners = concrete
1101		}
1102		if len(winners) > 1 {
1103			ids := make([]string, 0, len(winners))
1104			for _, c := range winners {
1105				ids = append(ids, c.route.ID)
1106			}
1107			sort.Strings(ids)
1108			f := failuref("route_conflict", "multiple routes match %s %s", req.Method, path)
1109			f.Candidates = ids
1110			return nil, f
1111		}
1112	
1113		upstreamURL, f := joinUpstream(winners[0].route, path, req.Target)
1114		if f != nil {
1115			return nil, f
1116		}
1117		return &Resolution{RouteID: winners[0].route.ID, UpstreamURL: upstreamURL}, nil
1118	}

1120	// methodMatch reports whether the method list matches the request method
1121	// concretely (an exact, case-sensitive entry) or via the "*" wildcard.
1122	func methodMatch(methods []string, method string) (concrete, wildcard bool) {
1123		for _, m := range methods {
1124			switch {
1125			case m == "*":
1126				wildcard = true
1127			case m == method:
1128				concrete = true
1129			}
1130		}
1131		return concrete, wildcard
1132	}

1134	// prefixMatch matches raw encoded paths on segment boundaries: "%2F" is never
1135	// treated as a separator and the root prefix matches every origin-path.
1136	func prefixMatch(prefix, path string) bool {
1137		if prefix == "/" {
1138			return true
1139		}
1140		if path == prefix {
1141			return true
1142		}
1143		return strings.HasPrefix(path, prefix) && path[len(prefix)] == '/'
1144	}

1146	// joinUpstream strips the route prefix from the request path and joins the
1147	// remainder onto the upstream base path with exactly one slash at the
1148	// junction. The junction is one run of literal slashes: every trailing
1149	// slash on the base path and every leading slash on the remainder are
1150	// merged into that single slash, even when either side contributes
1151	// several. Nothing else is normalized: slashes inside either part, the
1152	// remainder's trailing slashes (once non-slash content has appeared),
1153	// ".", ".." and percent escapes such as "%2F" are carried over byte for
1154	// byte, never decoded first. The base path is sliced out of the raw
1155	// upstream so joining never re-encodes, reorders or drops anything
1156	// outside the junction. The raw query is preserved verbatim unless the
1157	// route defines queryTransforms, in which case they rewrite it after
1158	// route selection.
1159	func joinUpstream(route *Route, path, target string) (string, *Failure) {
1160		if _, err := url.Parse(route.Upstream); err != nil {
1161			// Config validation already rejected this.
1162			return "", failuref("invalid_config", "route %q has an invalid upstream: %v", route.ID, err)
1163		}
1164	
1165		var remainder string
1166		switch {
1167		case route.PathPrefix == "/":
1168			// Root keeps the whole following path; "/" itself has an empty remainder.
1169			if path != "/" {
1170				remainder = path
1171			}
1172		default:
1173			remainder = path[len(route.PathPrefix):] // "" or "/...", boundary is a literal slash
1174		}
1175	
1176		// Slice the validated upstream raw so nothing outside the junction is
1177		// normalized or re-escaped. The address boundaries come from the same
1178		// splitUpstream reading the host validators used (scheme://authority
1179		// followed by the base path), so joining can never split userinfo, the
1180		// IPv6 brackets, the port or the base path differently than validation.
1181		parts := splitUpstream(route.Upstream)
1182		basePath := parts.basePath
1183	
1184		// Collapse only the junction run: all trailing slashes of the base
1185		// path meet all leading slashes of the remainder, and the junction
1186		// keeps exactly one slash whether or not anything follows them. A
1187		// remainder made entirely of slashes has no content past the run, so
1188		// it likewise ends in that single slash.
1189		baseTrimmed := strings.TrimRight(basePath, "/")
1190		rest := strings.TrimLeft(remainder, "/")
1191		joined := baseTrimmed + "/" + rest
1192	
1193		result := route.Upstream[:parts.schemeEnd+3] + parts.authority + joined
1194		query, f := applyQueryTransforms(route.QueryTransforms, target)
1195		if f != nil {
1196			return "", f
1197		}
1198		return result + query, nil
1199	}

1201	// validateTargetCharacters enforces on the raw target that only percent
1202	// encoding may carry a space or a control character: a direct ASCII space
1203	// (U+0020), a C0 control byte (U+0000 through U+001F) or DEL (U+007F) is
1204	// rejected no matter whether it sits in the path, a parameter name or a
1205	// parameter value. Bytes inside a well-formed percent escape ("%" plus two
1206	// hex digits) are skipped, so "%20", "%0A" and "%09" keep parsing and
1207	// matching on the raw encoded form; the rule never decodes an escape first.
1208	// Invalid percent escapes are owned by validPercentEscapes, which runs
1209	// before this check, so a lone or malformed "%" keeps its existing reason.
1210	// The reason names the first offending character as U+XXXX.
1211	func validateTargetCharacters(target string) *Failure {
1212		for i := 0; i < len(target); i++ {
1213			c := target[i]
1214			if c == '%' && i+2 < len(target) && isHex(target[i+1]) && isHex(target[i+2]) {
1215				// Skip a well-formed escape so an encoded space or control byte
1216				// is judged as data, never as a direct character. A malformed
1217				// escape is skipped byte by byte here; it is owned by the
1218				// validPercentEscapes check, which keeps its own earlier
1219				// reporting and must not let a following space be jumped over.
1220				i += 2
1221				continue
1222			}
1223			if c == ' ' || c < 0x20 || c == 0x7f {
1224				return failuref("invalid_request",
1225					"target contains a character that must be percent-encoded: U+%04X is not allowed to appear directly (percent-encode it, e.g. %%20 for a space)",
1226					c)
1227			}
1228		}
1229		return nil
1230	}

1232	// isToken reports whether s is an RFC 7230 token, i.e. a legal HTTP method.
1233	func isToken(s string) bool {
1234		if s == "" {
1235			return false
1236		}
1237		for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
1238			if !isTokenChar(s[i]) {
1239				return false
1240			}
1241		}
1242		return true
1243	}

1245	func isTokenChar(c byte) bool {
1246		switch {
1247		case c >= 'a' && c <= 'z', c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z', c >= '0' && c <= '9':
1248			return true
1249		}
1250		switch c {
1251		case '!', '#', '$', '%', '&', '\'', '*', '+', '-', '.', '^', '_', '`', '|', '~':
1252			return true
1253		}
1254		return false

1257	// validPercentEscapes checks that every "%' is followed by two hex digits.
1258	// Matching and joining stay on raw strings, but malformed escapes are rejected
1259	// up front for both prefixes and request targets.
1260	func validPercentEscapes(s string) bool {
1261		for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
1262			if s[i] != '%' {
1263				continue
1264			}
1265			if i+2 >= len(s) || !isHex(s[i+1]) || !isHex(s[i+2]) {
1266				return false
1267			}
1268			i += 2
1269		}
1270		return true
1271	}

1274		switch {
1275		case c >= '0' && c <= '9', c >= 'a' && c <= 'f', c >= 'A' && c <= 'F':
1276			return true
1277		}
1278		return false

8	// This file pins, as regression coverage, which error ParseConfig selects and
9	// where it points when several errors coexist in one configuration document.
10	// The rules under test are the existing accept/reject rules; the precedence
11	// they rely on is layered in Config.UnmarshalJSON:
12	//
13	//  1. JSON syntax (a broken document is only ever a parse failure),
14	//  2. the routes element type and the id/methods/pathPrefix/upstream field
15	//     types (type errors),
16	//  3. queryTransforms array and rule validity (rule errors),
17	//  4. field contents such as a non-absolute pathPrefix, a bad method token or
18	//     an empty id (content errors, in Config.validate).
19	//
20	// Within one layer the earliest array position wins: routes by their position
21	// in the routes array and rules by their position in the route's
22	// queryTransforms array, never by id ordering. Every failure must hand back no
23	// config at all, so no half-parsed configuration can ever resolve a request.

25	// expectInvalidConfig parses src and requires an invalid_config Failure whose
26	// reason contains every want substring and none of the forbidden substrings,
27	// and requires ParseConfig to hand back no config. It returns the Failure for
28	// any extra, test-specific assertions.
29	func expectInvalidConfig(t *testing.T, src string, want, forbidden []string) *Failure {
30		t.Helper()
31		cfg, f := ParseConfig([]byte(src))
32		if f == nil {
33			t.Fatalf("expected invalid_config, config was accepted: %s", src)
34		}
35		if f.Code != "invalid_config" {
36			t.Fatalf("code = %q, want invalid_config", f.Code)
37		}
38		if cfg != nil {
39			t.Fatalf("a rejected config must not be returned (no half config to resolve with), got %+v", cfg)
40		}
41		for _, sub := range want {
42			if !strings.Contains(f.Reason, sub) {
43				t.Fatalf("reason = %q, want substring %q\nconfig: %s", f.Reason, sub, src)
44			}
45		}
46		for _, sub := range forbidden {
47			if strings.Contains(f.Reason, sub) {
48				t.Fatalf("reason = %q must not contain %q\nconfig: %s", f.Reason, sub, src)
49			}
50		}
51		return f
52	}

329	//	step 3: pathPrefix repaired               -> accepted; route selection,
330	//	        upstream joining and query rewriting all work, and a route without
331	//	        transforms keeps the raw query byte for byte.

335		   "queryTransforms":[{"op":"frob","name":"a"}]},

345		   "queryTransforms":[

347		     {"op":"remove","name":"flag"},

349		   ]},
350		  {"id":"orders","methods":["GET"],"pathPrefix":"/api/orders","upstream":"http://orders.internal"}
351		]}`

353		  {"id":"api","methods":["GET"],"pathPrefix":"/api","upstream":"http://api.internal/v1",
354		   "queryTransforms":[
355		     {"op":"set","name":"a","value":"1"},
356		     {"op":"remove","name":"flag"},

358		   ]},

# 智能合约审计与形式化验证流水线

## 用途

合约产物与 ABI 管理、静态规则与模式库、符号执行与模糊测试编排、不变式检查、缺陷归因与报告版本化。

本仓库是可持续演进的自托管 Go 应用。领域核心位于 `contractsentinel/`，命令入口位于 `cmd/contractsentinel/`。

```bash
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel demo
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel version
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel resolve <config-file> < request.json
go test ./...
```

## 离线路由解析（resolve）

`resolve` 从配置文件读取路由，从标准输入读取一个 JSON 请求，在本机离线
完成匹配并输出命中的路由与上游地址，全程不建立网络连接。

配置文件：

```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"id": "api",  "methods": ["GET"], "pathPrefix": "/api", "upstream": "http://api.internal/v1"},
    {"id": "root", "methods": ["*"],  "pathPrefix": "/",    "upstream": "https://fallback.internal/base/"}
  ]
}
```

请求（`target` 为带可选查询串的路径）：

```json
{"method": "GET", "target": "/api/orders/7?a=1&a="}
```

成功时标准输出：

```json
{"routeId":"api","upstreamURL":"http://api.internal/v1/orders/7?a=1&a="}
```

匹配规则：

- `methods` 为非空数组，元素是区分大小写的具体 HTTP 方法名或 `*`（匹配任意合法方法）。
- `pathPrefix` 以 `/` 开头，除根前缀 `/` 外不能以 `/` 结尾，不含查询串或片段。
- 前缀按原始编码与请求路径匹配，并必须落在路径段边界上：`/api` 匹配
  `/api` 与 `/api/orders`，不匹配 `/apiv2`；`%2F` 不视为分隔符。
- 查询串不参与匹配。多条命中时最长前缀优先；前缀相同则具体方法优先于 `*`；
  仍有多条候选时返回 `route_conflict`，候选 `id` 按字典序排列；无候选返回
  `route_not_found`。
- 命中后去掉请求路径前缀，剩余路径接到 upstream 基础路径之后，连接处恰好
  保留一个 `/`（剩余路径为空也保留）；根前缀 `/` 保留其后全部路径。连接处
  以外的路径、百分号编码与原始查询串（含重复参数、空值与顺序）逐字节保留。

### queryTransforms 查询串改写

每条路由可新增 `queryTransforms` 数组，在路由选定之后、路径拼接完成后按
数组顺序改写查询串；匹配、冲突判定与路径拼接均不受其影响。省略该字段或给
空数组时，原始查询串逐字节保留。规则形如：

```json
"queryTransforms": [
  {"op": "set",    "name": "a",    "value": ""},
  {"op": "remove", "name": "flag"},
  {"op": "rename", "name": "old",  "to": "new"}
]
```

- `op` 仅支持 `set`、`remove`、`rename`；`name` 为非空字符串，按字面值使用。
- `set` 必须提供字符串 `value`（允许空字符串）；`remove` 不接受 `value`。
- `rename` 必须提供非空字符串 `to`，不接受 `value`；`name` 与 `to` 按
  字面值使用。命中的参数在原位置改名，各自的值、数量与相对顺序保留；
  已经叫目标名的参数继续保留，不合并也不覆盖。无等号的参数改名后仍无
  等号，空值保留等号；只重新编码被改动参数的名称（编码方式与 `set`
  相同），等号及其后的内容逐字节保留，值中的 `+`、百分号转义、额外等号
  与大小写都不改写。例如 `old=1&new=9&%6Fld=%2f+&old&x=` 把 `old`
  改名为 `new` 后得到 `new=1&new=9&new=%2f+&new&x=`。没有来源参数时
  查询串完全不变；`name` 与 `to` 相同时也不改写已有的名称编码。
- 查询串只以 `&` 分隔，第一个 `=` 分开名称和值；没有 `=` 的片段也能按名称
  命中。空查询串（`?` 后为空）视为没有片段，其余空片段（如 `?a=1&` 末尾）
  保留且不作为参数。
- 比较参数名称时解码百分号转义、把 `+` 视为空格、区分大小写，不做其他
  归一化；未命中名称的参数与其原始内容、顺序保持不变。
- `remove` 删除该名称的全部参数。`set` 把该名称的全部参数合并为一个，
  放在首次命中的位置；原查询中不存在时追加到末尾。没有查询串时 `remove`
  不产生问号，`set` 会创建查询串；原先的空问号在没有实际修改时保留，
  删除命中参数后若参数与空片段均已清空则去掉问号。
- 新增或替换的参数写成编码后的 `name=value`：仅 ASCII 字母、数字及
  `-._~` 原样出现，其他 UTF-8 字节使用大写百分号转义，空格写为 `%20`。
- 后一条规则基于前一条规则的结果执行。例如查询串
  `x=%2f&a=1&%61=2&flag` 先 `set a=""` 再 `remove flag`，结果为
  `x=%2f&a=`。`rename` 同样按数组次序串接：后续对目标名的 `set`
  仍合并所有同名参数，`remove` 仍删除全部同名参数。

数组或规则为 `null`、字段类型错误、未知操作、空名称、缺少必要字段、
`remove` 带 `value` 或 `rename` 缺少/带非法 `to` 或带 `value`，都使
整个配置返回 `invalid_config`（即使出错路由不会被命中）；reason 定位到
路由，规则错误另给出从 1 开始的规则序号。

失败时标准错误输出含 `code`、`reason` 的 JSON（`route_conflict` 另含
`candidates`），退出状态非零，标准输出不留下结果：

- `invalid_config`：配置不可读、JSON 无效或任一路由不合法（含非法
  queryTransforms；能定位时指出第几条路由及 id，规则错误指出规则序号）。
  合法 JSON 但结构不符与语法损坏严格区分：最外层必须是 JSON 对象，
  数组、字符串、数字、布尔值和 null 都被拒绝，reason 说明配置必须是
  对象并指出实际收到的类型，不猜测路由序号；对象中只要提供 `routes`
  就必须是数组，其他类型（含 null）报 `routes` 类型错误，不能当成没有
  路由；没有 `routes` 键的对象与 `"routes": []` 仍是合法空路由配置，
  合法请求对其解析得到 `route_not_found`。`routes` 数组的每个元素必须
  是对象，null 也按元素类型错误处理（不报缺少 id），reason 指出从 1
  开始的路由序号、要求的对象类型和实际收到的类型，且即使请求只会命中
  较早的合法路由，后面的非对象元素也会使整份配置被拒绝。
  合法 JSON 中某条路由的 `id`、`methods`、`pathPrefix`、`upstream`
  字段类型本身不符（如 `methods` 写成字符串、数组元素不是字符串）时，
  reason 直接指出从 1 开始的路由序号与字段，而非把整份配置说成无效
  JSON；该路由同时提供了合法非空字符串 `id` 时附带该 id（即使它写在
  出错字段之后），但 `id` 自身类型错误时只报位置与字段。只有 JSON
  语法损坏才报解析失败（即使开头包含 `routes` 或完整的第一条路由），
  且不猜测出错字段或路由位置；配置结构错误与请求错误同时存在时先报告
  `invalid_config`。此外，`upstream` 用方括号包围主机时，括号内必须是合法
  IPv6 地址（完整写法、压缩写法、含 IPv4 尾段均可），允许带端口、用户信息
  与区域标识（`%25eth0`）；空括号、括号内为普通名称或 IPv4 地址（如
  `[not-an-ip]`、`[127.0.0.1]`）及格式错误的 IPv6 地址都使整份配置返回
  `invalid_config`，reason 指出从 1 开始的路由序号、id 与 `upstream` 字段，
  说明括号中的主机不是合法 IPv6 地址，而不是把配置 JSON 说成语法损坏；普通
  域名与不带方括号的 IPv4 主机不受影响。反过来，IPv6 字面量主机必须完整放
  在一对方括号内，端口写在括号之外（如 `http://[2001:db8::1]:8080/base`）：
  完整写法、压缩写法、含 IPv4 尾段及带 `%25eth0` 区域标识的地址，不加括号都
  被拒绝，`http://2001:db8::1/base`、`http://::1:8080/base` 与
  `http://::ffff:192.0.2.1/base` 均属此类，末尾是数字也不能使其成为合法配置
  （主机与端口边界有歧义时不猜测端口，也不自动补括号），带端口或用户信息的
  写法同样拒绝；reason 指出从 1 开始的路由序号、该路由 id 与 `upstream` 字段，
  说明 IPv6 主机缺少方括号，这是地址内容错误而非配置 JSON 语法损坏，且只检查
  主机段——用户信息或基础路径中出现冒号不影响判定。此外，每个上游都必须真正
  填写非空主机：`http://:8080/base`、`https://:8443`、`http://:/base` 都使
  整份配置返回 `invalid_config`，即使主机位置前带有用户名或密码（如
  `https://user:p%40ss@:8443/v1`）也相同——用户信息、端口和基础路径都不能
  补足缺失的主机，也不会补上任何默认地址；判断的是主机有没有填写，端口格式
  仍沿用现有规则，所以有主机的 `http://api.internal:/base`（空端口）继续按
  现有行为接受。reason 指出从 1 开始的路由序号、该路由 id 与 `upstream`
  字段，并说明上游缺少主机，既不能说成配置 JSON 解析失败，也不能说成 IPv6
  缺少方括号；配置中只要有一条路由存在此问题，即使当前请求只会命中较早的
  合法路由，整份配置也在读取时被拒绝。
- `invalid_request`：方法缺失或不合法、`target` 不以 `/` 开头、含片段、非法百分号转义，
  或直接出现不允许的字符（ASCII 空格、U+0000 至 U+001F 控制字符、U+007F，无论位于路径、
  参数名称还是参数值）。该字符检查在路由选择与查询串改写之前进行：没有路由命中、路由冲突，
  或 `remove`、`set` 会删除/覆盖携带该字符的参数时，仍返回 `invalid_request`；reason 指出
  target 含有不允许直接出现的字符，并以 U+XXXX 形式说明最先出现的那个字符（JSON 中的
  `\n`、`\t`、`\u0000` 等转义解码后按此规则处理）。百分号编码与直接字符严格区分：
  `/api/orders%20next` 与 `/api/orders?note=%0A%09` 继续按现有规则解析，路径中的编码不先
  解码再匹配，未改写的编码、参数顺序与空格写法保持原样，不删除控制字符后继续解析；中文等
  未涉及该规则的内容保持现有行为。
  只有 JSON 语法损坏才报解析失败，且不猜测哪个字段出错；合法 JSON 但最外层是
  数组、数字、字符串、布尔值或 null 时，reason 说明请求必须是 JSON 对象；合法
  对象中 `method` 或 `target` 写成数字、布尔值、对象、数组或 null 时，reason
  指出该字段必须是字符串并说明收到的类型（null 算类型错误，不是字段未填写），
  两个字段都出错时先报告 `method`，与字段书写顺序无关；空字符串仍是内容问题
  （方法必填、目标路径必须以 `/` 开头），不归为类型错误。
- `route_conflict` / `route_not_found`：见上。

smart-contract-audit, formal-verification, symbolic-execution, fuzzing, security, exploit-analysis, reentrancy

Go 1.26，仅使用标准库，全部行为可在本机 CPU 上离线复现。

# 智能合约审计与形式化验证流水线

## 用途

合约产物与 ABI 管理、静态规则与模式库、符号执行与模糊测试编排、不变式检查、缺陷归因与报告版本化。

本仓库是可持续演进的自托管 Go 应用。领域核心位于 `contractsentinel/`，命令入口位于 `cmd/contractsentinel/`。

```bash
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel demo
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel version
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel resolve <config-file> < request.json
go test ./...
```

## 离线路由解析（resolve）

`resolve` 从配置文件读取路由，从标准输入读取一个 JSON 请求，在本机离线
完成匹配并输出命中的路由与上游地址，全程不建立网络连接。

配置文件：

```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"id": "api",  "methods": ["GET"], "pathPrefix": "/api", "upstream": "http://api.internal/v1"},
    {"id": "root", "methods": ["*"],  "pathPrefix": "/",    "upstream": "https://fallback.internal/base/"}
  ]
}
```

请求（`target` 为带可选查询串的路径）：

```json
{"method": "GET", "target": "/api/orders/7?a=1&a="}
```

成功时标准输出：

```json
{"routeId":"api","upstreamURL":"http://api.internal/v1/orders/7?a=1&a="}
```

匹配规则：

- `methods` 为非空数组，元素是区分大小写的具体 HTTP 方法名或 `*`（匹配任意合法方法）。
- `pathPrefix` 以 `/` 开头，除根前缀 `/` 外不能以 `/` 结尾，不含查询串或片段。
- 前缀按原始编码与请求路径匹配，并必须落在路径段边界上：`/api` 匹配
  `/api` 与 `/api/orders`，不匹配 `/apiv2`；`%2F` 不视为分隔符。
- 除百分号编码外，前缀中不得直接出现 ASCII 空格（U+0020）、U+0000 至
  U+001F 控制字符或 U+007F：请求 target 本身也禁止直接携带这些字符，
  因此含这种字符的前缀不可能被任何合法请求命中，配置在读取时即返回
  `invalid_config`。判定基于 JSON 解码后的字符串，直接写空格与写
  ` ` 失败方式相同，`\n`、`\t` 等转义也不能绕过；reason 指出
  pathPrefix、从 1 开始的路由位置、该路由合法的非空 id 与前缀中最先
  出现的违规字符（U+XXXX）。不删除字符、不修剪前缀、也不替用户补上
  百分号编码。`%20`、`%09`、`%00` 等合法百分号编码不是直接出现的字符，
  继续按原始文本处理，不先解码再检查或匹配：以 `/a%20b` 为前缀的路由
  仍能匹配 `/a%20b/items`。
- 查询串不参与匹配。多条命中时最长前缀优先；前缀相同则具体方法优先于 `*`；
  仍有多条候选时返回 `route_conflict`，候选 `id` 按字典序排列；无候选返回
  `route_not_found`。
- 命中后去掉请求路径前缀，剩余路径接到 upstream 基础路径之后，连接处恰好
  保留一个 `/`（剩余路径为空也保留）；根前缀 `/` 保留其后全部路径。连接处
  以外的路径、百分号编码与原始查询串（含重复参数、空值与顺序）逐字节保留。

### queryTransforms 查询串改写

每条路由可新增 `queryTransforms` 数组，在路由选定之后、路径拼接完成后按
数组顺序改写查询串；匹配、冲突判定与路径拼接均不受其影响。省略该字段或给
空数组时，原始查询串逐字节保留。规则形如：

```json
"queryTransforms": [
  {"op": "set",    "name": "a",    "value": ""},
  {"op": "remove", "name": "flag"},
  {"op": "rename", "name": "old",  "to": "new"}
]
```

- `op` 仅支持 `set`、`remove`、`rename`；`name` 为非空字符串，按字面值使用。
- `set` 必须提供字符串 `value`（允许空字符串）；`remove` 不接受 `value`。
- `rename` 必须提供非空字符串 `to`，不接受 `value`；`name` 与 `to` 按
  字面值使用。命中的参数在原位置改名，各自的值、数量与相对顺序保留；
  已经叫目标名的参数继续保留，不合并也不覆盖。无等号的参数改名后仍无
  等号，空值保留等号；只重新编码被改动参数的名称（编码方式与 `set`
  相同），等号及其后的内容逐字节保留，值中的 `+`、百分号转义、额外等号
  与大小写都不改写。例如 `old=1&new=9&%6Fld=%2f+&old&x=` 把 `old`
  改名为 `new` 后得到 `new=1&new=9&new=%2f+&new&x=`。没有来源参数时
  查询串完全不变；`name` 与 `to` 相同时也不改写已有的名称编码。
- 查询串只以 `&` 分隔，第一个 `=` 分开名称和值；没有 `=` 的片段也能按名称
  命中。空查询串（`?` 后为空）视为没有片段，其余空片段（如 `?a=1&` 末尾）
  保留且不作为参数。
- 比较参数名称时解码百分号转义、把 `+` 视为空格、区分大小写，不做其他
  归一化；未命中名称的参数与其原始内容、顺序保持不变。
- `remove` 删除该名称的全部参数。`set` 把该名称的全部参数合并为一个，
  放在首次命中的位置；原查询中不存在时追加到末尾。没有查询串时 `remove`
  不产生问号，`set` 会创建查询串；原先的空问号在没有实际修改时保留，
  删除命中参数后若参数与空片段均已清空则去掉问号。
- 新增或替换的参数写成编码后的 `name=value`：仅 ASCII 字母、数字及
  `-._~` 原样出现，其他 UTF-8 字节使用大写百分号转义，空格写为 `%20`。
- 后一条规则基于前一条规则的结果执行。例如查询串
  `x=%2f&a=1&%61=2&flag` 先 `set a=""` 再 `remove flag`，结果为
  `x=%2f&a=`。`rename` 同样按数组次序串接：后续对目标名的 `set`
  仍合并所有同名参数，`remove` 仍删除全部同名参数。

数组或规则为 `null`、字段类型错误、未知操作、空名称、缺少必要字段、
`remove` 带 `value` 或 `rename` 缺少/带非法 `to` 或带 `value`，都使
整个配置返回 `invalid_config`（即使出错路由不会被命中）；reason 定位到
路由，规则错误另给出从 1 开始的规则序号。

失败时标准错误输出含 `code`、`reason` 的 JSON（`route_conflict` 另含
`candidates`），退出状态非零，标准输出不留下结果：

- `invalid_config`：配置不可读、JSON 无效或任一路由不合法（含非法
  queryTransforms；能定位时指出第几条路由及 id，规则错误指出规则序号）。
  合法 JSON 但结构不符与语法损坏严格区分：最外层必须是 JSON 对象，
  数组、字符串、数字、布尔值和 null 都被拒绝，reason 说明配置必须是
  对象并指出实际收到的类型，不猜测路由序号；对象中只要提供 `routes`
  就必须是数组，其他类型（含 null）报 `routes` 类型错误，不能当成没有
  路由；没有 `routes` 键的对象与 `"routes": []` 仍是合法空路由配置，
  合法请求对其解析得到 `route_not_found`。`routes` 数组的每个元素必须
  是对象，null 也按元素类型错误处理（不报缺少 id），reason 指出从 1
  开始的路由序号、要求的对象类型和实际收到的类型，且即使请求只会命中
  较早的合法路由，后面的非对象元素也会使整份配置被拒绝。
  合法 JSON 中某条路由的 `id`、`methods`、`pathPrefix`、`upstream`
  字段类型本身不符（如 `methods` 写成字符串、数组元素不是字符串）时，
  reason 直接指出从 1 开始的路由序号与字段，而非把整份配置说成无效
  JSON；该路由同时提供了合法非空字符串 `id` 时附带该 id（即使它写在
  出错字段之后），但 `id` 自身类型错误时只报位置与字段。只有 JSON
  语法损坏才报解析失败（即使开头包含 `routes` 或完整的第一条路由），
  且不猜测出错字段或路由位置；配置结构错误与请求错误同时存在时先报告
  `invalid_config`。此外，`upstream` 用方括号包围主机时，括号内必须是合法
  IPv6 地址（完整写法、压缩写法、含 IPv4 尾段均可），允许带端口、用户信息
  与区域标识（`%25eth0`）；空括号、括号内为普通名称或 IPv4 地址（如
  `[not-an-ip]`、`[127.0.0.1]`）及格式错误的 IPv6 地址都使整份配置返回
  `invalid_config`，reason 指出从 1 开始的路由序号、id 与 `upstream` 字段，
  说明括号中的主机不是合法 IPv6 地址，而不是把配置 JSON 说成语法损坏；普通
  域名与不带方括号的 IPv4 主机不受影响。反过来，IPv6 字面量主机必须完整放
  在一对方括号内，端口写在括号之外（如 `http://[2001:db8::1]:8080/base`）：
  完整写法、压缩写法、含 IPv4 尾段及带 `%25eth0` 区域标识的地址，不加括号都
  被拒绝，`http://2001:db8::1/base`、`http://::1:8080/base` 与
  `http://::ffff:192.0.2.1/base` 均属此类，末尾是数字也不能使其成为合法配置
  （主机与端口边界有歧义时不猜测端口，也不自动补括号），带端口或用户信息的
  写法同样拒绝；reason 指出从 1 开始的路由序号、该路由 id 与 `upstream` 字段，
  说明 IPv6 主机缺少方括号，这是地址内容错误而非配置 JSON 语法损坏，且只检查
  主机段——用户信息或基础路径中出现冒号不影响判定。此外，每个上游都必须真正
  填写非空主机：`http://:8080/base`、`https://:8443`、`http://:/base` 都使

- `invalid_request`：方法缺失或不合法、`target` 不以 `/` 开头、含片段、非法百分号转义，

# 智能合约审计与形式化验证流水线

## 用途

合约产物与 ABI 管理、静态规则与模式库、符号执行与模糊测试编排、不变式检查、缺陷归因与报告版本化。

本仓库是可持续演进的自托管 Go 应用。领域核心位于 `contractsentinel/`，命令入口位于 `cmd/contractsentinel/`。

```bash
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel demo
go run ./cmd/contractsentinel version
```
